design_name: Bullet Strike deck missile launchers - FINAL (Tocandira / Caipora / Mula-sem-Cabeça)
philosophy: Tiro, porrada e bomba, with A's engine and A's numbers. Three crewed, power-free deck launchers - RAM micro-missile box (early), twin octagonal pods with a sensor dome (mid), headless quad battery with 48 tips (late) - run one loop: crew fill an internal magazine per resource family, a crewed autoloader fills the visible cells, a full rack ripples one dramatic salvo, then the launcher reloads. Sustained DPS sits exactly on the mod's tier bands; the drama is in the alpha and in the missiles: the Piranha school, the Carrapato countdown, napalm that keeps burning, EMP, the Boto decoy torpedo and the Iara nuke that must be masked. Overclock buys reload speed with heat, vented missiles and cook-off risk; the endgame battery is very powerful and very costly (5x6, 8 crew, 18 CP, 77000 cr, 2 per ship in the nuclear pool). Only vanilla component types and vanilla missile parts on the default path; every risky mechanic has a fallback that changes no number.
base_choice: BASE = Design A's launcher core (Model B latch, crewed autoloader, ModeSwitchDelay, DryFlush, safe napalm, untargetable limpet, heat per part loaded) and A's numeric spine (bands, OC <= 550, 300/400/600 m, 1500 drain per EMP part) - the two judges that weigh engine risk and balance both picked it (8.5 / 8.0). GRAFTED from B (fidelity 8.5): the stage-to-reference roster (RAM box -> twin octagonal pods + dome -> quad 3x4 battery), the Mula-sem-Cabeça endgame, the Piranha parameters (25 m, InheritVelocity false, weak late homing), the Iara in bs_limit_nuke with no OC, one magazine per resource family, per-family cook-off, the complete turret sketch and CrewKillChance on the limpet. GRAFTED from C: the micro-missile cassette (as Burst 2), the Boto decoy torpedo, the OC vent cost (scaled per cell), magnet + spacing children, the buzz-droid limpet charge, threshold MultiResourceStorage toggles, the isolated Repeating variant pattern and the counter matrix. NEW here: per-mode ModeSwitchDelay, tick-aligned ripples, heavy 16-unit layout on the Mula, children HP pool >= carrier HP, Iara masking timing.

launch_logic.model: NGEN Model B: crew-filled family magazine -> crewed autoloader -> ready-rack latch -> rippled salvo -> reload (vanilla component types only)
flow: 1. Crew carry vanilla missile parts into ONE magazine per resource family (HE / thermal / EMP / nuke) - the user's 'internal storage space for missiles'. Consumers request only the family the selected mode uses.

2. While (and only while) the launcher is crewed, the selected mode's AUTOLOADER moves one missile (PARTS parts -> 1 rack unit) every RELOAD seconds into the READY RACK. Vanilla reload timers keep counting unmanned; ours stop (gaps §4.4 #2).

3. The rack is a LATCH (thruster_boost battery pattern): it opens only when every cell is loaded and stays open until the last cell fired, so a salvo always completes and an overclocked loader can never turn it into endless fire.

4. The turret fires one cell every RIPPLE through a per-mode ModeCycle in LIFO order, so the ResourceSprites overlays match the real rack on every FULL salvo (the cycle restarts LIFO-aligned whenever the rack refills). Known cosmetic limit (T21): a partial DryFlush salvo, or the rest of an interrupted salvo after switching back into its mode, starts at the last cell, so one tube looks empty while a loaded-looking one fires; every emitter draws from the same ReadyRack_k, so counts and damage are unaffected.

5. Switching INTO a mode starts that mode's ModeSwitchDelay (= one full reload of that mode, OC-divided): a pre-filled second rack can never give two salvos back to back, also when the switch happens mid-salvo. A rack that is ALREADY FULL (latched) at the switch also waits PrefilledDelay_k = one full reload WITHOUT the overclock divide (variant prefilled_switch), because it was loaded without paying the overclock heat: racks pre-filled before combat give no free overclocked cadence.

6. When the family magazine has not been able to load one more missile of the mode for DRY_DELAY = CELLS x RELOAD seconds in a row (no crew delivery during a whole un-overclocked reload), the partial rack still fires (DryFlush, debounced by a ValueTween ramp + ThresholdToggle 100 %, chaingun ShellChangingValueTween pattern) - nothing is ever stranded, and a late crew trip never turns the latched rippled salvo into a trickle of mini-salvos (any delivery resets the wait).
7. Interrupted salvo: the latch stays on and the remaining cells go to the next target, then the launcher reloads.

8. Cook-off: one ScorchedEffects/DeathEffects pair PER STORAGE (each family magazine and every rack), outside the toggled blocks, each scaled by its own fill and weighted by its capacity in parts (BaseValue = family full-stock value x storage parts / cookoff.parts_full; a rack holds CELLS x PARTS parts): every stored part is worth value/parts_full wherever it sits, and magazine + largest rack full gives exactly the spec value; a scorched or destroyed loaded launcher explodes.

missile_types.special_behaviour: The user's 'Transformers 3' missile. Opens only 25 m from the hull (Discord value) so it never 'transforms' over our own deck; children leave at 40 m/s in a +-25 deg cone with late, weak homing + magnet + spacing, so they land on several parts. Children's HP pool >= carrier HP, so splitting never makes interception easier. Trades 10 % sustained damage for multi-part spread and for taxing the defender's ammo; in the reference LOCK model it leaks about as well as HE against one PD/CIWS (see balance_checks.interception).
missile_types.counterplay: Kill carriers before 25 m; big-radius area flak eats the child clumps (Pororoca r7, vanilla flak); shields catch the whole brood at the bubble; armor stops the small blasts.

resources_factories.decision: NO new resource and NO new factory in v1. Every missile uses a vanilla missile part, as the user asked ('pega o padrão que já tem no jogo'). The vanilla factories feed the launchers; parts can be bought or salvaged; SW:ACD launchers use the same IDs (missile_part_he/emp/nuke), so a combined game shares factories and nothing collides. Napalm runs on missile_part_thermal (vanilla since 0.30.0, never used by SW) and gets its own copper + sulfur chain. The Iara uses missile_part_nuke, never the Boiúna's Nuclear Shell chain.
resources_factories.in_game_tip: 1 HE Factory feeds 2 Caiporas or 5 Tocandiras; a Mula needs 1.8 HE Factories (2.6 with Stampede); a Mula on Poraquê needs 2.3 EMP Factories.
resources_factories.power_note: The launchers use no power (mod rule for weapons); the vanilla factories do - that is the vanilla missile economy.
resources_factories.factory_efficiency_decision: DECIDED: accept the vanilla missile economy. A vanilla HE factory feeds ~5300-6300 effective DPS of our HE missiles against ~1270 per factory in our guns' magazine chain (4-5x). Per ammo credit and per crew trip the missiles are in line or hungrier, and they pay with interception, crew, cook-off risk and long crewed reloads. SW:ACD and vanilla use the same parts at the same efficiency, so a factory-hungrier Bullet Strike missile would look weak next to them. Damage is NOT the lever. Lever kept for later (v2): a rafaeltessaro.bs_msl_canister resource (vanilla parts + 1 Standard Magazine, power-free press) would raise factory load without touching any damage number.

balance_checks.emp_reading: 1500 drain per EMP part (vanilla 2000), <= 750 SW shield HP per tile per second, and no salvo erases a SW giga bubble (320000): Caipora salvo 120000 (pops SW large 80000 - noted alpha), Mula salvo 180000. The EMP autoloader overclocks only / 1.2, so the overclocked rate stays under the mod's plasma OC cap of 880.
shields: Every missile is SimpleHit (penetration 0): it pops on the bubble edge, so against SW bubbles HE salvos are shield-breakers first (Caipora 112000, Mula 360000, Boto 4 x 36000 operational).
Piranha: the carrier opens on the bubble and children spend themselves on it (no bypass). Carrapato: no stick on shields, only the pop (43 % of HE). Taturana: generator heat + blast.
balance_checks.interception_model: Judge model (VERDICT_balance §2.6), extended: launch at max range, constant acceleration; PD shot latency 0.3 s, PD keeps its target (earliest impact) until it dies or impacts; airburst defenders at real trigger rates; LOCK = all airbursts of a trigger land on one target and catch up to lock_catch members of its clump (children / decoys); RETARGET = every airburst picks a fresh target (pessimistic bound for missiles); children spawn at 25 m with HealthFactor; torpedo decoys spawn at 1.5 s, half fly just ahead of the warhead. Multi-defender scenarios run every mount in parallel on the same salvo. Ideal aim, no overkill waste -> real swarms leak more.
interception_reading: EARLY: one Tocandira salvo leaks 58 % past ONE vanilla PD (target 40-60 %), 0 % past two; 380 HP = 3 vanilla PD shots; 12 micro-missiles 1/15 s apart.
MID HE vs one Tamanduá: 62 % under LOCK, 0 % under RETARGET - the CIWS model decides almost everything (test T10).
PIRANHA (mid): 88 % vs one vanilla PD, 92 % vs Tatu, 56 % vs Tamanduá LOCK: about HE's share (within ~6 points) at 90 % of HE's damage, spread over many parts; big-radius flak is its counter.
MULA HE: 56 % of 48 heads through the layered late defense (Pororoca + 2 Tamanduá + 2 vanilla PD) - the 48-missile stampede is the strongest saturation tool in the roster.
TORPEDOES: the late Boto leaks 50 % past one Tamanduá (6500 HP needs two triggers, decoys spend triggers) and 0 % past the layered defense; Iara 0 % alone against any CIWS/heavy flak - by design.
SW PD4 (1250 per shot) erases mid salvos; only the Mula saturates it. Intended: SW missiles (7000-9800 HP) stay the strongest missiles in SW; ours stay at vanilla scale.
balance_checks.combined_arms_reading: Iara pair launched first, masking salvo launched 1-3 s later (heavy missiles fly ~3.8 s to 600 m, torpedoes ~7.8 s): both warheads land through the layered late defense with a Mula HE mask at +1 s / +2 s. Same time or later = both die. Timing is the skill (B's 'tiro, porrada e bomba' hook, with the timing corrected).
logistics_reading: HE crew trips/min: Tocandira 3.97, Caipora 10.13, Mula 36.44 (our guns: Carcará 3.75, Tambor 8.33, Trovão 16, Mapinguari 30); vanilla HE launcher 12 trips/min for 3750 effective DPS = 3.2 trips per 1000 effective DPS; ours 3.2-3.75.
HE factories: 0.2 / 0.51 / 1.82; RecCrew (vanilla formula) 3.6 / 8.8 / 32.3 - the Mula needs a real logistics deck.

Internal stock = rack + 2 salvos of parts per family = 3 salvos: 27 s (Tocandira), 57 s (Caipora), 47 s (Mula HE) of fire; our guns hold 12-32 s - missiles carry more because the crewed reload is the real limiter and a full stock is a cook-off liability.
balance_checks.cookoff_reading: ~850 explosive per stored HE part (band 600-1000; vanilla 3333 over 12 parts): Tocandira 15300 at 18 parts, Caipora 81600 at 96, Mula 240000 at 288 + 96000 more with nuclear parts aboard. A loaded Mula is the ship's most dangerous part. Every storage (family magazine and each rack, a rack missile = PARTS parts) has its own cook-off pair weighted by its capacity in parts, so a part is worth the same in the magazine or in a rack and magazine + largest rack full gives exactly these numbers (stage 4; the stage 1-3 single Stock_<family> fill fraction over magazine + all racks under-stated them, e.g. Caipora HE 0.70, Mula Iara 2/34).
balance_checks.napalm_reading: Fire does at most 28 damage/s per burning tile (DAMAGE_PER_TICK 7 every 0.25 s at full value) until the part scorches; even if a whole salvo's tiles burn unattended, napalm stays below HE per tile -> it is not a hidden DPS mode. Zero on armor/structure.

user_presentation_ptbr:
## Lança-mísseis de convés do Bullet Strike - proposta final

Três lançadores, um para cada fase. Todos são torres de convés (em cima do casco), operados só pela tripulação e **sem energia**.

### Como funciona (igual nos três)
- **Estoque interno:** cada lançador tem um paiol por tipo de peça (HE, térmica, PEM, nuclear). A tripulação carrega as peças de míssil do jogo base até ele. O estoque cheio dá 3 salvas.
- **Recarga automática:** um autocarregador passa um míssil por vez do paiol para as células visíveis. **Só funciona com tripulação no posto.** Com todas as células cheias, sai a salva em sequência e a recarga recomeça. Se o paiol acabar, a salva parcial sai mesmo assim.
- **Trocar de míssil não dá salva grátis:** ao trocar o tipo, o lançador espera um ciclo completo de recarga do tipo novo.
- **Overclock (só meio e fim):** a recarga fica 1,5 vez mais rápida (PEM: 1,2 vez). Custos: calor por peça carregada (precisa de radiador), cerca de 1 em cada 16 mísseis é descartado a cada salva, pausa de 3 s ao desligar, o paiol esvazia mais rápido e, sem radiador, o lançador esquenta, pega fogo e explode junto com o estoque. Nunca acelera o torpedo nuclear.
- **Lançador cheio é uma bomba:** destruído ou queimado, explode proporcional ao estoque (cerca de 850 de dano por peça HE guardada).

### Os lançadores
- **Início - Tocandira (Caixa de Micromísseis de Convés), 2x2, 1 tripulante.** Caixa estilo RAM com 6 cassetes de tubo duplo: 12 micromísseis em 0,73 s a cada 9,1 s, alcance 300 m. Mísseis: Muriçoca (alto-explosivo) e Taturana-mirim (incendiário). Contra um PD vanilla, cerca de 58 % da salva passa.
- **Meio - Caipora (Lançador de Mísseis de Convés de Casulo Duplo), 3x3, 2 tripulantes.** Dois casulos octogonais e uma cúpula com olho sensor: 16 mísseis em 2 s a cada 19,0 s, alcance 400 m. Mísseis: Jararaca, Piranha, Carrapato, Taturana, Poraquê e o torpedo Boto (2 por salva). Overclock: Fúria da Caipora.
- **Fim - Mula-sem-Cabeça (Bateria Pesada de Mísseis Quádrupla), 5x6, 8 tripulantes, 18 CP, 77000 créditos.** Corpo sem cabeça com quatro casulos de 3x4 em braços hidráulicos: 48 mísseis pesados em 3,1 s a cada 15,8 s, alcance 600 m. Tem todos os mísseis, inclusive o nuclear Iara. Divide a vaga nuclear com a Boiúna (no máximo 2 por nave, em qualquer combinação). Overclock: Estouro da Boiada.

### Os mísseis
- **Jararaca (Alto-Explosivo):** explosão padrão; é o míssil "normal" do SW. Em salva grande, satura a defesa de ponto.
- **Piranha (Submunições, o "Transformers 3"):** abre a 25 m do casco e solta 4 (meio) ou 6 (fim) minimísseis que se espalham e acertam várias peças. Faz 90 % do dano do HE. O contra é flak de área de raio grande.
- **Carrapato (Grudento):** se for abatido no voo, perde-se; se acertar o casco, gruda, pisca e explode 2,5 s depois, com 50 % de chance de matar a tripulação que vier consertar. Não gruda em escudo.
- **Taturana (Napalm):** explosão pequena, fogo garantido na peça atingida e calor em volta que continua acendendo incêndios. Extintor, espuma e blindagem são o contra.
- **Poraquê (PEM):** drena bateria e escudos em área (1500 por peça PEM, abaixo do PEM vanilla). Não afeta as armas do Bullet Strike.
- **Boto (Torpedo com Iscas):** torpedo lento e resistente que solta 4 a 6 iscas para enganar a defesa de ponto. Faz 24000 (meio) ou 48000 (fim) de dano explosivo.
- **Iara (Torpedo Nuclear, só na Mula):** 120000 + 40000, 2 por salva a cada 20 s. Sozinho morre para qualquer flak; dispare o Iara primeiro e uma salva HE 1 a 3 s depois para os dois chegarem juntos.

### O que é arriscado e precisa de teste no jogo
1. **Carrapato:** a carga grudar num navio que gira e acelera. Há 4 planos B com os mesmos números.
2. **Piranha:** os filhotes herdarem o alvo e não estourarem sobre o nosso casco. Plano B: ímã para o casco inimigo e atraso maior.
3. **Trava das células** (salva completa antes de recarregar). Plano B com temporizador.
4. **Mísseis sobre o próprio convés:** não podem bater na nossa torre nem desviar do nosso casco.
5. **Nosso CIWS contra os nossos mísseis**, e o modelo do CIWS (cada disparo mata 1 míssil ou vários). Isso muda os números de interceptação.
6. **Desempenho** com muitas submunições; **torpedo com iscas** (dois disparos no mesmo evento); **vaga nuclear** dividida com a Boiúna.

Todas as mecânicas usam componentes do jogo base, a categoria 'missile' (compatível com o SW:ACD) e funcionam no 0.30.4 e no 0.30.5. Cada risco tem um plano B que não muda nenhum número.
